items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the bishop on c1 can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop on c1 can reach exactly a3, b2, d2, e3, f4, g5 and h6.
Bd1 is not a legal move: d1 is not on a diagonal from c1.
Bc2 is not a legal move: c2 is not on a diagonal from c1.

hints: Look at where the bishop can go along a diagonal from c1. What colour are the squares on those diagonals?
The bishop starts on a dark square. Check the colour of each square you tap.
Every reachable square is on a diagonal from c1, so none is a light square. d1 and c2 are not on one.
items.explain: The bishop moves only along diagonals, so every square it can reach from c1 has the same colour as c1. The validator confirms the seven squares and that Bd1 and Bc2 are illegal.

feedback_by_move.c1d1: Bd1 is illegal. d1 is a light square and the bishop stays on dark squares; it cannot change the colour of the squares it stands on.
feedback_by_move.c1c2: Bc2 is illegal: a bishop moves along diagonals, not straight like a rook or a pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move; no theme is named.

claims.statement: Bxc1 is a legal move.
Bxe7 is not a legal move: the pawn on c5 blocks the diagonal.
Bxc1 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Bxc1 wins at least four points of material along the engine line.

hints: Trace each diagonal from the bishop square by square. Where does a piece stand in the way?
On the long diagonal a piece stands on c5. What happens to the squares beyond it?
One enemy piece is on the short diagonal and nothing blocks the way to it.
items.explain: The bishop cannot jump: the pawn on c5 blocks the diagonal, so Bxe7 is illegal. The rook on c1 sits on the free diagonal, and Bxc1 wins it. The validator confirms the legality claims and the engine result.

feedback_by_move.a3e7: Bxe7 is illegal: a bishop cannot jump over the pawn on c5. It could only take the pawn itself.

items.prompt: White to move. A black knight stands right in front of the bishop. Find the move that wins material.

claims.statement: Bxe5 is not a legal move: a bishop does not capture straight ahead.
Bxb7 is a legal move.
Bxb7 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Bxb7 wins at least four points of material along the engine line.

hints: Which squares can the bishop reach from e4? List the diagonals.
The square directly in front is not on any of them.
Look along the long diagonal towards the top left.
items.explain: A bishop moves and captures only along diagonals, so the knight straight ahead on e5 cannot be taken: Bxe5 is illegal. The rook on b7 is on a diagonal, and Bxb7 wins it.

feedback_by_move.e4e5: Bxe5 is illegal: a bishop never moves or captures one square straight ahead. Look at the diagonals.

items.prompt: Black to move. The pawn on g2 has not moved yet. Can the black king still catch it? Find the only move that draws.

claims.statement: After Kf4 the result is a draw.
After Ke4 Black loses.
After Kd4 Black loses.

hints: Count the moves the pawn needs from g2 to the last rank. Remember what a pawn may do on its first move.
If you count six pawn moves you will think there is a spare move. Is there?
Only one king move keeps the draw. It steps toward the pawn's file and the squares it will pass.
items.explain: A pawn on its starting square may advance two squares on its first move, so it needs one move fewer than a count of single steps suggests. The tablebase shows Kf4 as the only drawing move; Ke4 and Kd4 lose.

feedback_by_move.e3e4: Ke4 looks close enough if you count six pawn moves, but the tablebase says it loses. Count again with the pawn's two-square first move.
feedback_by_move.e3d4: Kd4 loses according to the tablebase. Count the pawn's moves again, allowing its first move to be two squares.

items.prompt: Black to move. Can the black king stop the pawn on d2? Find the only move that draws.

claims.statement: After Ke4 the result is a draw.
After Kf4 Black loses.
After Kg4 Black loses.

hints: The king must reach the pawn's path in time. What does one step in each direction gain?
A step straight up the board gains a rank only. Which step gains a file and a rank at once?
Look at the diagonal step toward the pawn's file.
items.explain: A diagonal king step gains a file and a rank in a single move, so it can be the only step that keeps the king in time. The tablebase shows Ke4 draws; Kf4 and Kg4 lose.

feedback_by_move.f3f4: Kf4 walks straight up the board and gains one rank only. The tablebase says it loses; the diagonal step Ke4 is the move that draws.
feedback_by_move.f3g4: Kg4 moves away from the pawn's file, and the tablebase says it loses.

items.prompt: White to move. A tablebase has classified every move here. Which single move wins?

claims.statement: After Kc4 the result is a win for White.
After e5 the result is a draw.
After Kb4 the result is a draw.

hints: Test the natural move first: ask what the table would say about pushing the pawn.
Several moves draw and one wins. The table gives a verdict for each move but no reason.
The winning move is a king move toward the pawn.
items.explain: The tablebase gives an exact verdict for each move: Kc4 wins, while the pawn push e5 and Kb4 only draw. It does not say why. The reason has to be worked out by a person, for instance by changing the position and asking the table again.

feedback_by_move.e4e5: e5 is the natural-looking move, but the tablebase says the game is only a draw after it. The table reports that result; it does not give the reason.
feedback_by_move.b3b4: Kb4 only draws according to the tablebase. It names the verdict, not the reason.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move; no theme is named.

claims.statement: Now one white piece attacks g7.
Now one black piece defends g7.
After Qg4 two white pieces attack g7.
Qg4 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Nxg7 is at least three pawns worse than Qg4.
Qg4 wins material along the engine line.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of g7 now. Then ask what each side can bring there in one move.
One white piece can reach the g-file in a single move.
The count is one against one now. Which move makes it two against one?
items.explain: Counting only what attacks g7 now gives one against one, and taking at once with Nxg7 loses at least three pawns' worth. Qg4 brings a second attacker, so the count on g7 becomes two against one. The validator confirms the counts and the engine result.

feedback_by_move.f5g7: Nxg7 uses the count as it stands, one attacker against one defender, and the engine rates it at least three pawns below Qg4. Ask what can arrive first.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move; no theme is named.

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack d5.
Two black pieces defend d5.
exd5 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Nxd5 is at least one and a half pawns worse than exd5.
exd5 wins at least two points of material along the engine line.

hints: Count attackers and defenders on d5. Do the numbers differ?
The counts are equal. What else differs between the pieces that would capture first?
The cheapest capturer should go first.
items.explain: The counts on d5 are equal, two against two, but the pieces are not: the pawn is worth less than the knight, so capturing with it first changes the result. The engine rates exd5 best and Nxd5 at least one and a half pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.c3d5: Nxd5 captures first with the more valuable piece. The counts are equal, but the engine rates it at least one and a half pawns below exd5.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has a pawn on e4 in the centre. Find the best move; no theme is named.

claims.statement: Nxd4 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Nxe4 is at least three pawns worse than Nxd4.
Nxe4 is a legal move.

hints: Before you take the centre pawn, list what recaptures on e4 and what else is in the position.
Taking the pawn at once is one option among several. Check what it costs.
Another capture, on a different square, works better.
items.explain: Capturing the centre pawn at once is not forced. The engine rates Nxe4 at least three pawns below Nxd4, so the quick capture is not the move here.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: Nxe4 takes the centre pawn at once, but the engine rates it at least three pawns below Nxd4. A mobile centre pawn does not have to be taken immediately.

items.prompt: White to move. Imagine your opening notes end here with the tempting capture Nxf7. Check before you play it: find the best move.

claims.statement: Nxf7 is a legal move.
Bxd4 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Nxf7 is at least three pawns worse than Bxd4.

hints: Ask whether the move in your notes still works in this exact position, not the one you studied.
Look at the black pieces near the centre. Which one can be taken?
Capture the bishop on d4.
items.explain: Preparation that stops at the opening leaves nothing to rely on once the game leaves the notes, and the habit of checking each move is part of readiness. Here the engine rates Nxf7 at least three pawns below Bxd4.

feedback_by_move.e5f7: Nxf7 may be the move your notes show, but the engine rates it at least three pawns below Bxd4. A prepared move still has to be checked in the position on the board.

items.prompt: White to move. One move takes a pawn and attacks two black pieces at once. Is it the best? Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxb7 is a legal capture.
After Bxb7 one white piece attacks the rook on a8.
After Bxb7 one white piece attacks the bishop on c8.
Bb4 is the engine's best move at depth 16.
Bxb7 is at least three pawns worse than Bb4.

hints: List what Bxb7 does. Then list what the other candidate moves do, one at a time.
A move that does several jobs is not automatically the best one. Check the cost of each job.
Look at the d6 square and what stands behind it.
items.explain: A move that pursues several goals at once is not better for that reason. Bxb7 takes a pawn and attacks two pieces, but the engine rates it at least three pawns below Bb4.

feedback_by_move.d5b7: Bxb7 takes a pawn and attacks two pieces, which is why it is tempting, but the engine rates it at least three pawns below Bb4. More goals in one move is not the same as a better move.
